notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise fintech prospect evaluating Redwood Dedicated on H100 for production support agent + internal knowledge assistant.
- They’re performance-sensitive and are pushing hard on consistency week-over-week ("no surprise regressions").
- Strong interest in Dedicated due to data isolation, predictable throughput, and ability to align with internal change management.

Primary use case / workload
- Chat-style customer support assistant + agent-facing summarization.
- Mix of short turns (prefill 0.5–2k tokens, decode 200–800 tokens) and periodic long-context jobs (prefill 16k–48k tokens, decode 500–1500 tokens).
- Concurrency: wants to start with 200–400 concurrent requests at peak across 2 regions, then scale.
- Model preferences: open models only. Mentioned Llama-class 70B / 8B for tiered routing. Wants deterministic fallback behavior (same family/quality band).

Performance requirements (what they said on calls)
- Latency: target p95 < 1.2s time-to-first-token for typical chat turns; p99 must stay stable during traffic bursts.
- Throughput: cares more about stable tokens/sec at peak than raw max TPS; needs predictable headroom for incident days.
- Tail latency: biggest concern is p99/p99.9 blowups when long-context requests enter the same queue.
- Reliability: wants clear rollback procedure if a runtime/profile change causes regressions.

Dedicated H100 evaluation details
- Hardware: Dedicated H100 preferred (asked specifically about H100 SXM vs PCIe; we responded we can support both but will size/benchmark accordingly).
- Regions: US + EU in later phase; data residency will likely require EU region for a subset of traffic.
- Network: VPC peering required; they asked if we support customer-managed egress allowlists and private endpoints.

Key theme: profile pinning / change control
- Prospect explicitly requested ability to pin "known-good" performance settings during POC and early production.
- Quote (paraphrased): "We can’t have kernel/batching changes slip in under us without an explicit change window. If performance changes, we need a knob to roll back immediately."
- We discussed Redwood runtime’s hardware tuning profile pack direction:
  - Versioned profiles (profile_id + profile_version) per GPU SKU (H100) and workload shape.
  - Ability to pin profile_version in Dedicated with guardrails + auditability (no silent drift).
  - Rollback semantics: revert profile version (and/or disable feature flag) without swapping the model or endpoint.
- Action item: provide a one-pager explaining pinning/rollout approach for Dedicated (what is pinned, what can still change with runtime upgrades, how we communicate deprecations).

Technical deep dive (Fireflies)
- Linked transcript: ff-981244-technical-deep-dive.
- Topics covered:
  - How we handle mixed prompt lengths (prefill vs decode scheduling) and what metrics we expose for queueing vs compute.
  - Kernel selection/fallback behavior on H100 and what would trigger kernel fallbacks.
  - Observability they want in the POC: active profile id/version, queueing time, and "why latency spiked" breakdown.

Security / compliance
- Requirements surfaced:
  - SSO/SAML for console access (mandatory).
  - Audit logs: need to export admin actions + config changes (esp. profile pins/overrides).
  - Retention controls: asked for retention window on request/response logs + ability to disable content logging.
  - KMS integration preferred for encryption at rest.
- They will run a formal security review; asked for SOC 2 report and architecture diagram of Dedicated isolation boundaries.
